summary: Full E2E testing of MidGate Preview #1. Backend: 25/26 pytest passed (96%). Frontend: all critical E2E flows pass (landing, register, dashboard, link creation, analytics nav, theme toggle, language toggle, protected route redirect). One real backend bug: brute-force lockout does not trigger because the identifier is scoped by `request.client.host`, but the k8s ingress load-balances requests across two backend pods with different upstream IPs (10.232.130.143 & 10.232.130.144), so no single identifier ever reaches the 5-attempt threshold. All other features (auth, tenant isolation, URL safety, redirect 302, analytics capture, billing plans) verified working.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout (429) does not trigger. identifier = f"{request.client.host}:{email}" in /app/backend/app/domains/auth.py:92 uses the direct socket peer. Behind the k8s ingress, requests round-robin between backend pod IPs (verified in MongoDB login_attempts: count splits across '10.232.130.143:email' and '10.232.130.144:email', each stays below 5). After 7 failed logins the account is still not locked. Fix: use X-Forwarded-For (first hop) or drop IP from identifier (email-only) or configure uvicorn --proxy-headers with FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*'.

critical_code_review_comments: auth.py brute-force identifier uses request.client.host which is not the real client behind the ingress — see action item above.
email_provider.send is awaited synchronously inside /api/auth/register; slow email providers would block registration. Consider background task / fire-and-forget.
links.py: no destination URL length limit (destination_url is `str` in Pydantic). Consider max_length to prevent oversized payloads.
MongoDB ObjectId handling — auth.py uses ObjectId(user_id) in refresh/reset, which will 500 if a malformed refresh token slips through. Wrap with try/except or use string _id.

brute-force lockup: locked_until is only stored as ISO string; verifying with datetime.fromisoformat works but reset behavior increments count indefinitely even after lock elapses — a first successful login after lock will still reset, which is fine, but consider expiring the counter.

Run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py -v. Key finding: brute-force lockout fails in preview env due to k8s ingress round-robin between 2 backend pods — verify in DB (db.login_attempts) — main agent needs to fix identifier logic in auth.py.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout bug RCA: In /app/backend/app/domains/auth.py the failure-attempt identifier is built as `f"{request.client.host if request.client else 'x'}:{email}"`. In the preview environment the Kubernetes ingress terminates the connection and load-balances the requests between two backend pods; `request.client.host` therefore alternates between the ingress-facing IPs seen by each pod (observed: 10.232.130.143 and 10.232.130.144). Because the identifier changes per hop, the counter is split across two documents in the login_attempts collection, and neither reaches the threshold of 5, so the 429 lockout never fires. Reproduction: register any user, then POST /api/auth/login with wrong password 7 times — all return 401, none return 429. Mitigation: (a) trust proxy headers — start uvicorn with --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*' and read `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for', '').split(',')[0].strip()`, or (b) drop the IP portion and key on email only (with a TTL), or (c) key on email + the first XFF hop.
